message: Vibrational analysis completed for water.xyz: 3 vibrational modes (3N-6 = 3, nonlinear), 0 imaginary. MINIMUM: no imaginary frequencies above 30 cm^-1. This geometry is a local minimum on the MACE potential energy surface. ZPE 0.5843 eV. Thermochemistry at 298.15 K / 101325 Pa with symmetry number sigma=2 (detected): G = -2081.0167 eV. IR intensities: UNAVAILABLE for this model. | Warnings: The submitted geometry was not a stationary point (max force 0.070088 eV/Å > 0.005 eV/Å), so it was relaxed with BFGS before the Hessian: 4 steps, max force now 0.000653 eV/Å. The frequencies, the energy and the positions below belong to the RELAXED geometry, not to the one submitted. IR intensities are NOT available for this model, so none are reported and no spectrum should be drawn from this result. The attached calculator (MACECalculator) does not declare 'dipole' in implemented_properties (it declares: energy, energies, free_energy, node_energy, forces, stress). ase.vibrations.Infrared derives IR intensities from dipole derivatives and requires calc.get_dipole_moment(atoms). MACECalculator only adds 'dipole' to implemented_properties when model_type is one of DipoleMACE / EnergyDipoleMACE / DipolePolarizabilityMACE (mace/calculators/mace.py:170-171). mace_mp() and mace_off() construct MACECalculator without passing model_type (mace/calculators/foundations_models.py:168-170 and 282-284), so it defaults to 'MACE' and implemented_properties is ['energy', 'energies', 'free_energy', 'node_energy', 'forces', 'stress'] — no dipole. Verified at runtime on this deployment: calc.get_dipole_moment() raises PropertyNotImplementedError. MACE-MP-0 and MACE-OFF therefore CANNOT produce IR intensities. Frequencies are exact and reported in full; intensities are null. A stick spectrum drawn with uniform or invented intensities would be a fabrication, so none is produced.

animation.note: displacementsAngstrom is the Cartesian normal-mode eigenvector rescaled so the largest single-atom displacement equals amplitudeAngstrom. Relative magnitudes and directions within a mode are physical; the overall scale is a display choice.

infrared.reason: The attached calculator (MACECalculator) does not declare 'dipole' in implemented_properties (it declares: energy, energies, free_energy, node_energy, forces, stress). ase.vibrations.Infrared derives IR intensities from dipole derivatives and requires calc.get_dipole_moment(atoms). MACECalculator only adds 'dipole' to implemented_properties when model_type is one of DipoleMACE / EnergyDipoleMACE / DipolePolarizabilityMACE (mace/calculators/mace.py:170-171). mace_mp() and mace_off() construct MACECalculator without passing model_type (mace/calculators/foundations_models.py:168-170 and 282-284), so it defaults to 'MACE' and implemented_properties is ['energy', 'energies', 'free_energy', 'node_energy', 'forces', 'stress'] — no dipole. Verified at runtime on this deployment: calc.get_dipole_moment() raises PropertyNotImplementedError. MACE-MP-0 and MACE-OFF therefore CANNOT produce IR intensities. Frequencies are exact and reported in full; intensities are null. A stick spectrum drawn with uniform or invented intensities would be a fabrication, so none is produced.

cost.schemeNote: 19 evaluations for the Hessian (6N displacements plus the equilibrium point), and 2 more for the gates: one for the entry fmax check and one uncached probe to measure the cost.

finiteDifference.note: Central differences: 6N+1 = 19 MACE force evaluations (ASE also evaluates the undisplaced geometry). Forward differences would cost 3N+1 but carry O(delta) error and assume exactly zero equilibrium forces, which a geometry converged only to 0.005 eV/Å does not provide.

thermochemistry.pressureNote: P = 101325 Pa. The default, 101325 Pa, is 1 atm — the reference state of most tabulated thermochemistry. It is not 1 bar (exactly 100000 Pa), which is the IUPAC standard state and the reference ase.thermochemistry uses internally; ASE applies the -kB*ln(P/1 bar) correction, worth +0.34 meV on G at 298.15 K.

symmetry.effectOnEntropy: sigma enters the entropy only as -kB*ln(sigma). At sigma=2 and T=298.15 K it lowers S by 5.973e-05 eV/K (5.76 J/(mol*K)) and raises G by 0.0178 eV relative to sigma=1. Every entropy and Gibbs number below is correct ONLY for sigma=2.

definitions.internalEnergyEv: U = H - kB*T (ideal gas, PV = kB*T per molecule)
definitions.enthalpyEv: H = E_pot + ZPE + Cv_trans*T + Cv_rot*T + dU_vib(T) + kB*T
definitions.entropyEvPerK: S = S_trans + S_rot + S_elec + S_vib + S(1 bar -> P)
